Compare Fractions: Interactive Practice

FractionsArithmetic
Game: Two fractions are shown; say whether the first is less than, equal to, or more than the second.
How to play: Press the <, = or > button under them. Tick Show graphics for bars, and Use common denominator to cut both bars into equal parts.

Look for the math

To compare a/c and b/d you can cross-multiply: a/c > b/d exactly when ad > bc. Or you can give them the same denominator and compare the numerators.

Two ways, one answer

Cutting both bars into the least common denominator’s parts (the tick box) turns the comparison into counting shaded parts: a/c = a·(L/c)/L and b/d = b·(L/d)/L. The logic test compared the two methods for every pair of fractions with parts up to 30 (810,000 pairs): they never differ.

What the practice gives you

The pairs are made as in the applet: denominators 5 to 9, numerators 5 to 9 or just under the denominator, one pair in about twenty with equal values written differently (like 2/3 and 4/6), so all three answers occur. The test checked 200,000 generated pairs. For quicker ways see the companion page, Fraction Comparison Sped Up.

Press Show graphics and compare 3/5 with 5/8, first with their own bars and then with the common denominator.
